A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BMLR study. Their complete text, equations, figures and appendices support comparison, including matching results relocated into v3's appendices.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic parameter-estimation experiments and CIFAR-10 image-correction results in Section 4, with additional norm-based evaluations in Appendix D.

after.justification: V3 retains original synthetic and CIFAR-10 experiments and reports additional parameter-scale checks, fitted convergence slopes and image-reconstruction analyses in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The least-squares estimate of C, averaging estimator for B, leave-one-row-out ratio and clipping for A, and sparse hard-thresholding procedures remain equivalent. V1's Equations (8)-(12) correspond to v3's Equations (3)-(6). Alternative normalization is discussed hypothetically, not introduced as an implemented procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate synthetic BMLR parameter recovery and CIFAR-10 image correction under the same multiplicative transformation model. The new coefficient-scale sweeps vary parameters within the existing synthetic generator, while SNR analyses retain the image-corruption setting. Non-orthogonal random designs were already used in v1.

E2.justification: Neither version reports experimental comparisons against KRO-PRO-FAC, alternating minimization or other cited estimation methods. The image experiments retain the same comparison between uncorrected noisy images and images corrected by the proposed estimators.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the reported default sample size from T=1000 to T=2000 and describes unsquared rather than squared Frobenius error. Appendix B adds coefficient-scale settings, explicit slope-fitting procedures and SNR-based image evaluation with a maximum-norm metric. The underlying experiment design and CIFAR-10 split remain intact; these disclosures do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V3 substantially extends validation beyond v1's qualitative dimension and noise sweeps: Appendix B.1 checks coefficient scales c=1,2,3,5; B.2 estimates convergence slopes and examines fit quality; B.3 examines global and local image errors against effective SNR. Synthetic operator- and maximum-norm evaluations themselves were already present in v1's Appendix D.

E5.justification: Appendix B.2 adds regression-based estimation of convergence slopes and goodness-of-fit reporting, including the statement that most R-squared values exceed 0.9. Image-result error bars remain standard deviations. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: V3 adds quantitative scaling results across dimensions and norms; Table 1 reports sample-size Frobenius slopes of -0.496 for A and -0.526 for B. Synthetic curves and aggregate image-distance curves are revised, and SNR/maximum-norm image results are added. V1's single-image distances 215.44 and 79.88 and its numerical recovery discrepancy within 10^-8 are omitted. Changed synthetic settings preclude interpreting the replacement curves as same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The principal recovery results, error bounds and sparse-support guarantees are retained. V3 replaces the undefined sigma_1 squared denominator in the A-bound statements with the defined tilde-sigma squared and removes explicit derivations of Mills' and Frechet inequalities while retaining their statements. Appendix A discusses possible extensions without proving new generalized error bounds.

C1.justification: The main contributions remain explicit estimators, individual finite-sample guarantees, sparse recovery and numerical validation. V3 removes v1's explicit claim to be the first comprehensive non-asymptotic analysis of each parameter and adds a more specific criticism that vectorized estimation has high variance when nmpq greatly exceeds T.

C2.justification: New Appendix A substantially expands discussion of orthogonality and isotropic-noise restrictions, possible individual relaxations and difficulties relaxing both simultaneously. Section 4.1 interprets performance outside ORT, while Appendix B.1 explains dimensional asymmetry through normalization and discusses normalizing B instead. These provide substantive applicability qualifications and mechanism explanations absent from v1.

D1.justification: V3 supplies coefficient-scale values, regression specifications and the effective-SNR calculation for its additional analyses. However, it removes v1's Python implementation statement and public BMLR GitHub access information. This establishes removal of reproducibility information from the paper, not disappearance of the repository.

R1.justification: The opening positioning shifts toward multivariate and trace regression, adding Chen et al. (2020), Kidzinski and Hastie (2024), and Klopp (2011), while removing several topic-model and structured-factor references. The principal related-work discussion of alternating minimization, spectral methods, KRO-PRO-FAC and autoregression remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, the separate model subsection is integrated into the introduction, and noiseless/noisy terminology becomes population/sample terminology. Estimator definitions receive a separate subsection, canonical-basis material moves into Appendix C, and the appendices are reorganized around new assumptions and numerical-analysis sections.

P2.justification: Separate estimator/norm plots are consolidated into multicurve panels, with logarithmic axes and revised legends. V3 adds Table 1 and two SNR figures, redraws the aggregate image plot, and substantially resizes the retained image example and main-text plots. Typography, margins and title-page styling also change throughout.

improvement.justification: V3 makes the central empirical validation more assessable through fitted sample-size slopes near -1/2 and clarifies the scope of the theory through Appendix A's assumptions discussion. These provide a limited net improvement while the method and principal guarantees remain stable. Benefits are tempered by removal of code-access information and inconsistencies between Appendix B.2's fitting specification, Table 1 caption and claims about norm-sensitivity ordering.
